event: Clashes between police and Joint Awami Action Committee supporters in Azad Kashmir resulted in 11 deaths including four police officers, dozens of injuries, and over 70 arrests.

verified_facts.statement: Clashes occurred between police and Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) supporters in Azad Kashmir (Rawalakot area).
verified_facts.note: Confirmed by multiple Pakistani news outlets and international reporting.

verified_facts.statement: The official death toll reported by AJK government is 11, including four police officers.
verified_facts.note: Government statement; the total is contested by JAAC and civil society sources.

verified_facts.statement: Over 70 arrests were made during and after the clashes.
verified_facts.note: Reported by Pakistani media; exact number varies slightly across sources.

verified_facts.statement: Dozens of injuries were sustained by both police and civilians.
verified_facts.note: Confirmed across multiple sources; exact count not universally specified.

verified_facts.statement: The JAAC was designated under Pakistan's Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) prior to the clashes.
verified_facts.note: Government proscription order issued; date and legal basis confirmed in official statements.

verified_facts.statement: AJK elections were scheduled for July 27, 2024, with candidate nomination opening days after the clashes.
verified_facts.note: Election calendar is a matter of public record.

verified_facts.statement: A communications blackout (mobile internet shutdown) occurred in AJK following the clashes.
verified_facts.note: NetBlocks and international media confirmed connectivity loss; duration and scope documented.

verified_facts.statement: The AJK assembly includes 12 reserved seats for 1947 Partition refugees.
verified_facts.note: Constitutional/electoral fact; confirmed in AJK governance documents.

verified_facts.statement: JAAC presented a 38-point charter of demands to the government.
verified_facts.note: Document exists and has been reported; specific demands are public.

verified_facts.statement: Four police officers were killed during the clashes.
verified_facts.note: Confirmed by government and independent sources; names and details documented.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: JAAC members fired live ammunition at police first.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed by State Security framing; disputed by Civil Rights framing. No independent ballistics or forensic evidence publicly available; communications blackout prevents independent verification.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: JAAC laid siege to a military hospital.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Asserted by State Security framing; not independently confirmed. Scope and nature of any occupation unclear amid information control.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: The actual death toll is significantly higher than 11 (claims range to 27+).
unverified_shared_claims.note: Alleged by Civil Rights and Information Control framings; unverified due to communications blackout and lack of independent access to morgues or medical records.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: India's government made public statements condemning the crackdown.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed by Geopolitical framing; MEA statements exist but their exact timing, wording, and characterization are contested.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Pakistan alleges Indian backing or instigation of JAAC protests.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Asserted by Geopolitical framing and some government officials; no public evidence provided; standard accusation in India-Pakistan disputes.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Previous reform agreements (2024, 2025) were not implemented by the government.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed by Governance Failure framing; specific agreements and their implementation status require documentary verification not yet publicly detailed.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Mangla Dam hydropower revenue is extracted while local residents lack affordable electricity.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Asserted by Governance Failure framing; requires detailed fiscal and utility data not independently verified in public sources.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Criminal cases were filed against journalists for reporting on the clashes.
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed by Information Control framing; some cases reported but full scope and charges require independent legal documentation.

points_of_disagreement: Whether JAAC fired first on police or police used excessive lethal force against unarmed/lightly-armed protesters.
Whether JAAC is a legitimate civil society movement or a terrorist organization warranting proscription.
The true death toll: official 11 vs. alleged 20+ by JAAC and civil society monitors.
Whether the government's ban on JAAC and crackdown timing (days before elections) was a lawful security operation or political suppression of electoral competition.
Whether the communications blackout was a necessary security measure or a deliberate strategy to obstruct accountability and independent verification.
Whether India's statements represent genuine concern for human rights or geopolitical opportunism; whether Pakistan's allegations of Indian instigation are credible.
Whether the 12 reserved refugee seats are a constitutional protection or an undemocratic mechanism enabling federal control of AJK.
Whether the root cause is JAAC's alleged terrorism/armed activity or chronic governance failure, resource extraction, and broken reform agreements.
Whether an independent international inquiry is necessary or whether domestic accountability mechanisms are sufficient.
shared_foundation.summary: All framings accept that clashes occurred in Rawalakot between police and JAAC supporters, resulting in at least 11 deaths (including four officers), dozens of injuries, over 70 arrests, and a communications blackout. The shared factual ground includes the election timing, the 38-point charter, the refugee-seat constitutional structure, and the proscription order. The disagreements center on causation (who fired first), legitimacy (protest vs. terrorism), true casualty figures (obscured by blackout), intent (security vs. suppression), and remedies (inquiry vs. domestic accountability).

framings.name: State Security / Law and Order
framings.question: Did JAAC members initiate armed violence against law enforcement, justifying a forceful security response?
framings.key_claim: The AJK government conducted a lawful, targeted security operation against an armed, terrorist-designated group that fired first on police officers and laid siege to a military hospital.
framings.description: This framing positions the JAAC as an organized violent actor whose members deliberately attacked security forces in a 'planned manner,' necessitating a limited police operation to restore order. It treats the anti-terrorism designation as legitimate and the deaths of four officers as evidence of the group's threatening nature.
framings.emphasizes: JAAC members' use of live fire against police, the deaths of law enforcement personnel, the proscription order's legal basis under the ATA, and the government's repeated offers of dialogue.
framings.downplays: Disproportionality of force against protesters, the broader civil-rights character of the movement, internet blackouts, and casualty disputes that suggest higher civilian deaths.
sample_headlines: Four law enforcers, three protesters killed in clashes over disputed refugee seats in Azad Kashmir — Arab News
AJK govt begins legal action against banned JAAC leaders over sedition allegations — Geo.tv

carriers.name: AJK Police / Home Department
carriers.excerpt: 'Since June 6, four law enforcement officials have been martyred in the firing by violent elements,' Azad Kashmir police said in a statement.
carriers.role_evidence: Official police statements and Home Department notification first framed JAAC as a proscribed terrorist organization responsible for initiating lethal violence.

carriers.name: Arab News PK
carriers.excerpt: Authorities accused JAAC members of opening fire on law enforcers in a 'planned manner,' laying siege to the Combined Military Hospital.
carriers.role_evidence: Prominent English-language regional outlet gave significant space to official AJK and police framing of the violence as premeditated JAAC aggression.

carriers.name: Geo TV
carriers.excerpt: AJK government declared JAAC a proscribed organisation under anti-terrorism laws, saying the group was 'engaged in terrorism, acting in a manner prejudicial to the peace and security of the State'.
carriers.role_evidence: Pakistan's largest Urdu/English broadcaster amplified the government's legal-security framing to a mass domestic audience.

carriers.name: AJK Government (PM Rathore)
carriers.excerpt: Prime Minister Rathore warned against 'mob rule' while JAAC vowed to proceed with its June 9 protest.
carriers.role_evidence: AJK PM formally adopted the state security frame by invoking anti-terror law and framing protests as threats to constitutional order.

carriers.name: Pakistan Defence Minister Khawaja Asif (via X)
carriers.excerpt: The demand to abolish the 12 seats, made ahead of the upcoming elections, is tantamount to sabotaging the electoral process.
carriers.role_evidence: Federal minister framed the protest's core demand as election sabotage, extending the security frame to the federal government level.

framings.name: Civil Rights / State Repression
framings.question: Did Pakistani authorities use disproportionate and unlawful force to silence a legitimate grassroots civil rights movement?
framings.key_claim: Pakistan's anti-terrorism designation of JAAC and the lethal crackdown on protesters in Rawalakot represent a systematic attempt to crush a legitimate civil society movement demanding economic relief and political rights.
framings.description: This framing foregrounds the JAAC as a broad-based, multi-stakeholder civil society coalition—traders, lawyers, students, women—whose demands for governance reform and economic equity are being answered with live ammunition, arrests, and an anti-terror label. It treats the proscription as a profound abuse of state power.
framings.emphasizes: Deaths of protesters, the ban on a grassroots organization, internet blackouts, mass arrests, the 38-point charter's legitimate demands, and the JAAC's non-violent self-identification.
framings.downplays: Deaths and injuries among police officers, any evidence of armed elements within protest crowds, and the government's claim that 36 of 38 demands had been agreed to.
sample_headlines: Pakistan: 'Terrorism' designation of protest movement marks dangerous escalation in Jammu and Kashmir crackdown — Amnesty International
AJK bans JAAC under Anti-Terrorism law as PM warns against 'mob rule' — VoicePK

carriers.name: Amnesty International
carriers.excerpt: 'Branding a grassroots organization as 'terrorist' on vague grounds, while simultaneously cutting the region off from the outside world, raises serious concerns.'
carriers.role_evidence: Amnesty International was the first major international human rights institution to formally frame the crackdown as a violation of rights of association and call for an independent inquiry.

carriers.name: Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP)
carriers.excerpt: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan said it was 'deeply alarmed' by the violence and questioned the use of anti-terror laws against the JAAC.
carriers.role_evidence: Pakistan's premier domestic human rights body issued public concern and announced a fact-finding mission, giving the civil rights framing domestic institutional legitimacy.

carriers.name: VoicePK
carriers.excerpt: Senator Afrasiab Khattak said banning a 'non-violent voice of the people' under anti-terrorism laws amounted to a gross violation of fundamental rights.
carriers.role_evidence: Independent Pakistani outlet gave prominent voice to civil society critics of the ban before the violence erupted, grounding the repression framing in domestic political opposition.

carriers.name: JAAC (Shaukat Nawaz Mir, via X/video)
carriers.excerpt: Mir accused the authorities of unleashing violence in Rawalakot, saying, 'The state has begun a massacre of our people in Rawalakot.'
carriers.role_evidence: JAAC leadership originated the 'massacre' language that seeded the repression framing in social media and diaspora networks before international outlets picked it up.

carriers.name: Kashmiri Diaspora UK (London, Bradford, Birmingham protests)
carriers.excerpt: Demonstrations in London, Bradford, Birmingham and Manchester condemned the 'brutal military suppression' of the peaceful civil rights movement.
carriers.role_evidence: Simultaneous diaspora protests across four UK cities gave the repression framing a transnational physical presence and media visibility beyond South Asia.

carriers.name: Republic World (Indian outlet)
carriers.excerpt: The ban comes amid mounting public anger against the Pakistani government, with local leadership accusing Islamabad of decades of betrayal.
carriers.role_evidence: Major Indian media outlet with a large English-language readership amplified the civil rights framing, though from a perspective sympathetic to anti-Pakistan narratives.

framings.name: Geopolitical / India–Pakistan Proxy Conflict
framings.question: Is the AJK unrest a reflection of — or ammunition for — the broader India-Pakistan territorial and diplomatic rivalry over Kashmir?
framings.key_claim: Both governments are instrumentalizing the violence: India to condemn Pakistan's 'police brutality' and press international accountability, while Pakistan alleges Indian-backed instigation behind the protests.
framings.description: This framing situates the domestic clashes inside the larger unresolved Kashmir dispute. Indian officials and media use the deaths to attack Pakistan's human rights record internationally. Pakistani officials, meanwhile, have hinted at Indian interference in the movement. Each side weaponizes the event to advance its geopolitical narrative.
framings.emphasizes: India's MEA statements, Pakistan's counter-accusations of foreign meddling, the Kashmir territorial context, and the event's potential impact on India-Pakistan diplomacy.
framings.downplays: The domestic economic and governance grievances of AJK residents as primary drivers; the agency of the JAAC as an independent local actor.
sample_headlines: India flags 'police brutality' in PoK, calls on international community to hold Pakistan accountable — India TV News
PoK Unrest: Deadly Clash Erupts Between Police and Protesters as Pakistani Authorities Launch Violent Crackdown — NewsGram

carriers.name: India MEA (Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson)
carriers.excerpt: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal criticised Pakistan for what he described as 'brutality' and 'severe police violence' against protesters in PoJK.
carriers.role_evidence: India's official government spokesperson was the first institutional actor to formally call out Pakistan internationally over the killings and demand international accountability.

carriers.name: NewsGram (India)
carriers.excerpt: India flagged the 'police brutality' in the regions and called upon international governments to hold Islamabad accountable for its 'misdeeds and abuses.'
carriers.role_evidence: Pro-India English-language outlet amplified the MEA framing to an international English-language audience, using 'Pakistan-occupied Kashmir' terminology throughout.

carriers.name: Outlook India
carriers.excerpt: 11 killed after JAAC ban sparks violent clashes in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir.
carriers.role_evidence: Major Indian national magazine consistently used 'Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir' framing, positioning the event as evidence of Pakistani state failure in a contested territory.

carriers.name: AJK / Pakistani officials (unnamed)
carriers.excerpt: Some officials in Muzaffarabad and Islamabad have publicly suggested that elements within the JAAC movement may be influenced or encouraged by India.
carriers.role_evidence: Pakistani officials counter-deployed the geopolitical frame by alleging Indian interference, attempting to delegitimize the domestic protest movement.

carriers.name: Senator Mushahid Hussain Syed (Pakistan)
carriers.excerpt: At a time when India was facing diplomatic challenges over its policies in Indian-administered Kashmir, Pakistan's officialdom had created a new crisis in sensitive Azad Kashmir.
carriers.role_evidence: Pakistani ex-senator pushed back on both sides of the geopolitical framing by arguing the ban hands India a propaganda victory and undermines Pakistan's own Kashmir narrative.

carriers.name: JURIST (legal news)
carriers.excerpt: The violent suppression of protests in AJK have drawn comparisons to conditions in Indian-administered Kashmir, potentially weakening Pakistan's moral stance.
carriers.role_evidence: Legal-academic outlet first systematically mapped how the crackdown complicates Pakistan's geopolitical Kashmir narrative, influencing later analysis.

framings.name: Electoral / Political Manipulation
framings.question: Is the timing of the ban and crackdown — six weeks before AJK elections — evidence of deliberate political suppression of opposition?
framings.key_claim: The government's decision to ban JAAC and escalate the crackdown days before July 27 elections and the opening of candidate nomination was designed to suppress political competition and entrench the Islamabad-backed establishment.
framings.description: This framing reads the anti-terror designation not as a security measure but as an electoral weapon, noting the extraordinary coincidence of the June 5 ban with the June 9 nomination period and July 27 polling date. It interrogates who benefits from JAAC's silencing.
framings.emphasizes: Election calendar timing, JAAC's claim that the 12 refugee seats allow PML-N/PPP to control AJK's government formation, and historical patterns of federal interference in AJK elections.
framings.downplays: Genuine security concerns, the pattern of violence in earlier JAAC protests, and the legal merits of the anti-terror designation.
sample_headlines: AJK bans JAAC under Anti-Terrorism law as PM warns against 'mob rule'; Committee says June 9 protest will go ahead — VoicePK
Tensions Escalate in PoK: Anti-Terror Law Invoked Against Civil Rights Alliance Ahead of June 9 Strike — Republic World

carriers.name: JAAC leadership (official statements)
carriers.excerpt: JAAC argued that the 12 seats allow Pakistan's mainstream political parties, particularly the PML-N and PPP, to influence government formation in Azad Kashmir.
carriers.role_evidence: JAAC itself originated the electoral-manipulation framing by explicitly linking the reserved-seat demand to Islamabad's control over AJK's political outcomes.

carriers.name: VoicePK
carriers.excerpt: The dispute intensified after the Election Commission announced that nomination papers for the July 27 elections would be filed from June 9, the same day JAAC plans to hold its wheel-jam strike.
carriers.role_evidence: Independent Pakistani investigative outlet was among the first to highlight the electoral timing coincidence in detail, making the political-manipulation framing explicit.

carriers.name: Republic World (India)
carriers.excerpt: The scheduled general elections for the final week of July 2026 are now heavily shadowed by this prolonged civil agitation.
carriers.role_evidence: Large Indian outlet amplified the electoral-manipulation angle to an international audience, framing it as evidence of Pakistani democratic dysfunction.

carriers.name: Arab News PK
carriers.excerpt: The dispute comes ahead of legislative elections scheduled for July 27 in the mountainous region.
carriers.role_evidence: Neutral regional outlet noted the electoral context without driving the framing, providing supporting factual scaffolding.

framings.name: Governance Failure / Elite Capture
framings.question: Do the protests expose a deeper structural failure of governance — elite privilege, unmet economic promises, and Islamabad's administrative stranglehold over AJK?
framings.key_claim: Recurring unrest in AJK reflects chronic governance failure: a captive political system propped up by refugee-seat quotas, unimplemented reform agreements, and an economy that extracts resources (like Mangla Dam hydropower) while denying local residents affordable electricity and wheat.
framings.description: This framing treats the clashes not as an isolated policing event but as a symptom of structural political-economic dysfunction. It focuses on the 38-point charter's systemic demands, the pattern of broken agreements, and elite privilege as root causes. Analysis-oriented, it is favored by academics, civil society researchers, and some quality journalism.
framings.emphasizes: The 38-point charter, broken implementation of 2024 and 2025 agreements, the hydro-power paradox, elite perks, Islamabad's de-facto control, and repeated protest cycles.
framings.downplays: The acute security crisis, individual culpability for violence, and geopolitical dimensions of the conflict.
sample_headlines: Why has Pakistan-administered Kashmir erupted in protest again? — Al Jazeera
Large-scale protests, police repression, and initial reforms reshape enabling environment in Azad Kashmir — Hivos/EU SEE

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: 'The current crisis reflects a broader and longer-term debate about governance, political representation, resource distribution, and regional autonomy in AJK,' Ahmed said.
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's explainer format and expert sourcing made it the main international conduit for the structural governance framing, reaching a global English-language audience.

carriers.name: Raja Qaiser Ahmed (Quaid-i-Azam University)
carriers.excerpt: 'This ruling effectively closed the legal route for groups seeking to challenge the existing arrangement and intensified calls for protest by the [JAAC].'
carriers.role_evidence: Islamabad-based area studies academic provided the governance-failure analytical framework that Al Jazeera and other outlets cited to contextualize the violence.

carriers.name: Hivos / EU SEE (civil society research)
carriers.excerpt: The 2025 protests have significantly reshaped the enabling environment in Pakistan administered Kashmir by exposing deep governance failures, eroding public trust, and simultaneously revitalizing civic mobilization.
carriers.role_evidence: International development/civil-society research platform produced a substantive governance-failure analysis of the 2025 protest cycle that pre-framed coverage of the 2026 escalation.

carriers.name: JURIST
carriers.excerpt: A local protest over government plans to drop subsidies for wheat and electricity rapidly transformed into a broader movement demanding comprehensive reform, accountability, and regional economic relief.
carriers.role_evidence: Legal journalism outlet analyzed the governance and rule-of-law dimensions with expert depth ahead of the 2026 escalation, establishing early analytical infrastructure.

carriers.name: Wikipedia (2025 Azad Kashmir protests article)
carriers.excerpt: Unlike previous protests that were largely sectoral or economic, this movement expanded into a multi-stakeholder campaign addressing structural governance issues.
carriers.role_evidence: Crowd-sourced reference article synthesizing the governance-failure framing is a top search result, diffusing this frame to a broad general-information audience.

framings.name: Use-of-Force / Accountability
framings.question: Was the use of live ammunition by security forces against protesters lawful under international human rights standards, and will there be accountability for killings on both sides?
framings.key_claim: The killing of at least six protesters by security forces—and disputed, potentially much higher, casualty figures amid a communications blackout—demands an independent, impartial inquiry into whether lethal force complied with international standards.
framings.description: Distinct from the broader civil-rights repression framing, this lens focuses narrowly on evidentiary and procedural questions: the rules of engagement, the sequencing of violence (who shot first), conflicting official/JAAC casualty tallies, and the feasibility of a credible probe given the internet blackout.
framings.emphasizes: Contested death tolls (official: 11; JAAC: potentially higher), the communications blackout obstructing verification, the killing of named individuals like Shahzeb Habib, and the call for an independent inquiry.
framings.downplays: Macro political causes of the unrest and geopolitical angles.
sample_headlines: Pakistan: 'Terrorism' designation of protest movement marks dangerous escalation — Amnesty International
At least 11 killed in Pakistan-administered Kashmir clashes before rally — Al Jazeera

carriers.name: Amnesty International (Isabelle Lassee)
carriers.excerpt: 'The authorities must conduct an independent inquiry into allegations of the extrajudicial killing of Shahzeb Habib.'
carriers.role_evidence: Amnesty's statement was the first to name an individual alleged extrajudicial killing and call for a specific independent accountability mechanism, originating this accountability sub-frame.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: 'Four police officers and a passer-by died after miscreants shot at them,' Sardar Waheed Khan told Reuters, while 'six protesters were killed' as the result of law enforcers' response.
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera juxtaposed official and JAAC accounts side-by-side, amplifying the evidentiary contradiction at the heart of the accountability framing.

carriers.name: NetBlocks (internet monitoring)
carriers.excerpt: NetBlocks said that its data showed that access to the web remained severely restricted in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
carriers.role_evidence: NetBlocks provided the technical evidence of the communications blackout that is central to the accountability framing — i.e., verifying that independent on-the-ground reporting was being suppressed.

carriers.name: Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP)
carriers.excerpt: The HRCP announced plans to send a fact-finding team to assess the situation on the ground.
carriers.role_evidence: HRCP's announced fact-finding mission institutionalized the accountability framing by committing organizational resources to independent verification.

carriers.name: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif office
carriers.excerpt: 'The Prime Minister, expressing deep concern over the unpleasant incidents, has ordered a transparent investigation into the incident.'
carriers.role_evidence: Government's own call for a 'transparent investigation' nominally adopted accountability language while critics questioned whether it would be genuinely independent.

framings.name: Refugee Rights / Representation Dispute
framings.question: Are the 12 reserved legislative seats for Kashmiri refugees a legitimate safeguard for a dispossessed minority, or a mechanism for political manipulation of AJK's democratic process?
framings.key_claim: The conflict over 12 reserved assembly seats is a genuine clash between the rights of 1947 Partition refugees to political representation and the democratic rights of AJK's resident population — a constitutional dispute the Supreme Court alone cannot resolve.
framings.description: This framing isolates the specific policy dispute — reserved seats for refugees from Indian-administered Kashmir — as the proximate legal and political trigger for the clashes. It presents both sides of the seats debate with nuance, examining refugee historical claims against JAAC's arguments about institutional capture.
framings.emphasizes: The AJK Supreme Court ruling that seats are constitutionally protected, refugee communities' Partition-era sacrifices and poverty, JAAC's 'fake State Subject certificates' allegations, and the constitutional amendment pathway.
framings.downplays: The broader economic and governance grievances that preceded the reserved-seats dispute, and the security response to the protests.
sample_headlines: Deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir: What's going on? — Al Jazeera
Four law enforcers, three protesters killed in clashes over disputed refugee seats in Azad Kashmir — Arab News PK

carriers.name: Al Jazeera (Raja Qaiser Ahmed and ministerial voices)
carriers.excerpt: 'These are the people whose families migrated from India, where they were landowners and businesspeople, but moved to Pakistan in abject poverty.'
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera gave substantial airtime to the refugee-rights counter-argument through direct ministerial quotes, making it the most balanced international carrier of this framing.

carriers.name: Arab News PK
carriers.excerpt: The unrest marks the most serious escalation yet in a months-long confrontation over 12 seats in the regional assembly reserved for refugees from Indian-administered Kashmir who settled in Pakistan after 1947.
carriers.role_evidence: Arab News consistently framed the violence through the reserved-seats dispute lens from the outset, providing structured policy context.

carriers.name: Pakistan Defence Minister Khawaja Asif (X / social media)
carriers.excerpt: In Sialkot, there is one seat in the Azad Kashmir Assembly reserved for migrant Kashmiris who sacrificed over 200,000 lives during partition.
carriers.role_evidence: Federal minister formally articulated the refugee-rights justification for retaining the seats in an institutional statement, embedding this counter-framing in government discourse.

carriers.name: JAAC leadership (statements & charter)
carriers.excerpt: JAAC claims these seats are filled using 'fake State Subject certificates' to benefit influential political figures rather than genuine stakeholders.
carriers.role_evidence: JAAC's counter-narrative explicitly challenged the refugee-rights frame by alleging the seats have been captured by political elites, not genuine refugees.

carriers.name: AJK Supreme Court
carriers.excerpt: The Supreme Court of Azad Jammu and Kashmir ruled that the 12 reserved seats are constitutionally protected and cannot be abolished without a constitutional amendment.
carriers.role_evidence: Court ruling directly triggered the clashes and institutionally validated the 'seats are legally protected' dimension of this framing, escalating the confrontation.

framings.name: Information Control / Digital Repression
framings.question: Is Pakistan's internet blackout and media suppression in AJK itself a form of violence — preventing accountability, distorting casualty figures, and silencing civil society?
framings.key_claim: The government's total communications blackout in AJK — blocking mobile internet, sealing the JAAC office, filing criminal cases against journalists — is a deliberate strategy to control the narrative and shield security forces from accountability during lethal operations.
framings.description: This framing foregrounds the information war around the event as much as the physical violence. It tracks the government's pre-emptive censorship tools (internet shutdowns, journalist prosecutions, 'fake news' warnings) as instruments of repression that compound the physical crackdown and obstruct independent verification of what happened in Rawalakot.
framings.emphasizes: NetBlocks data on connectivity blackout, suspended mobile services, criminal cases against journalists for 'fake news,' JAAC's sealed offices, and wildly divergent casualty figures (official: 11 dead vs. social-media claims of 27+).
framings.downplays: The government's argument that communications restrictions prevent further violence coordination, and the genuine disinformation risks in a fast-moving conflict.
sample_headlines: AJK region has seen an uptick in media censorship and repression of free speech — JURIST
Internet access remained severely restricted in Pakistan-administered Kashmir — NetBlocks/Al Jazeera

carriers.name: NetBlocks
carriers.excerpt: NetBlocks said that its data showed access to the web remained severely restricted in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
carriers.role_evidence: Internet-monitoring NGO provided objective technical data that originated the information-control framing with hard evidence rather than assertion.

carriers.name: JURIST
carriers.excerpt: The AJK government filed criminal cases against journalists under recently amended sections of the penal code for allegedly spreading 'fake news.'
carriers.role_evidence: Legal journalism outlet documented the journalist-prosecution dimension of information control in the 2025 cycle, pre-framing the 2026 coverage.

carriers.name: International Federation of Journalists (IFJ)
carriers.excerpt: The IFJ reported that amendments to the AJK penal code criminalize criticism of government officials and impose penalties of up to seven years' imprisonment.
carriers.role_evidence: Global journalists' federation institutionally adopted and documented the press-freedom/information-suppression framing around AJK.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: The government imposed a complete communications blackout, with residents cut off from mobile telecommunications and internet access.
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera consistently highlighted the connectivity blackout in both its 2025 and 2026 coverage, diffusing the information-control framing globally.

carriers.name: NewsGram / Pakistani journalists on X
carriers.excerpt: Pakistani media and journalists on X have said that the total death toll could be much higher.
carriers.role_evidence: Pakistani journalists using X to push back on official casualty figures amplified information-control concerns to a social-media audience, fueling the competing-claims dynamic.

gap_analysis: Missing are framings centered on: (1) Economic grievances and material conditions driving mobilization (unemployment, resource distribution, development disparities in Azad Kashmir); (2) Community/local perspectives from affected families, injured persons, and residents experiencing the aftermath; (3) International humanitarian law and documentation standards for casualty verification; (4) Intra-movement dynamics within JAAC itself (leadership disputes, tactical disagreements, factional tensions); (5) Police institutional perspectives beyond security framing (officer safety concerns, training gaps, command structure failures); (6) Religious or identity-based framings if relevant to JAAC's constituency or messaging; (7) Comparative analysis with similar clashes in disputed territories or Pakistan-administered regions.
